findings.issue: A failed per-session trace read replaced observed tree anomalies with empty arrays.
findings.disposition: Corrected partial polling and REST tree failure handling. Healthy sibling trace updates and recovery remain observable.

findings.issue: The source-selection matrix lacked a retained regression for denied access to a regular SQLite file.
findings.disposition: Added a Linux production server test. The unprivileged run passed and the privileged-runner code compiled.

findings.issue: An older pending REST trace response could overwrite a newer diagnostic without a test failure.
findings.disposition: Added the response-order regression and retained the existing behavior.

findings.issue: An unselected active session could keep an obsolete failure after a complete reconnect or fallback tree.
findings.disposition: Reconcile scoped source failures when the client accepts a complete current tree.

findings.issue: An older fallback tree request could erase a newer manual failure or reinstate an obsolete failure after recovery.
findings.disposition: Order fallback and manual tree observations together.

findings.issue: An older selected-trace source error could reappear after a newer complete tree demonstrated recovery.
findings.disposition: Reconcile source-read errors with successful complete observations for the affected session.

findings.issue: The cross-path diagnostic tests use identical successful trees and do not directly assert ordering of two different successful payloads.
findings.disposition: Accepted coverage limit. The test reviewer ran a distinct-payload probe that passed the candidate and caught a deliberately broken guard; retained tests cover diagnostic ordering and stale manual responses.
